SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    8662
H. J. C. R. Station,
REPORT
Date August 8, 19 38.

Subject S.I. T. J. G. C. I.D.

Made by d    Forwarded by D. I. GLOVER.

Sir,

During the evening of the 7th Aug. 1938, D. J. I. Uemoto of
the S.P.O. Staff, informed D.S.I. Maklaevsky that at 10 p.m.,
that day, the Japanese Gend merie required assistance in
raiding house situated in the West Hongkew District, in
order to arrest a member of Chinese Mobile Unit. From
information obtained by the Japanese Military it had been
ascertained that one named ZUNG TUNG NONG (陳冬濃),
residing at House No. 7, Lane 831 Tiendong Road, had supplied
money to Chinese Mobile Units operating in Kootung.

D.S.I. Maklaevsky relayed this request for assistance
to the undersigned, and it was arranged that a member of the
S.P.O. and party from the Japanese Gendarmerie should meet
the undersigned, D.S.I. Vung Ts Ming and detectives attached
to C.I., at West Hongkew Station, at 10 p.m., that evening.

At the appointed time the undersigned met D. J. Yamahara,
and a party of Gendarmes under Sergt. Major Kitoda, at West
Hongkew Station and having obtained the services of three
Chinese uniform policeman, proceeded to the address given.

On arrival, this address was found to be a large house
owned apparently by a Chinese of some affluence.

An elderly gentleman, Mr. Zung Ping Ki (陳丙麒), was
interviewed by the undersigned, who stated that the wanted
man, his younger brother, was away from Shanghai.

As the Japanese Gendarmerie insisted upon carrying
out a search for documentary evidence, a search of the wanted
man's room was carried out. No incriminating documents,

上海公共租界工部局警务处。    8662
虹口捕房，
报告
日期：1938年8月8日。

事由：S.I. T. J. G. C. I.D.

撰写人 d    转呈人：D. I. GLOVER。

先生：

1938年8月7日晚，特别政治股（S.P.O.）职员 D. J. I. Uemoto 告知副督察长 Maklaevsky，当晚10时，日本宪兵队要求协助搜查位于虹口西区的一处住宅，以逮捕一名中国流动部队成员。根据日军获得的情报，已查明一名名为 ZUNG TUNG NONG（陳冬濃）的人，居住在天潼路831弄7号，曾向在嘉定（Kootung）活动的中国流动部队提供资金。

副督察长 Maklaevsky 将此协助请求转达给本人，并商定由一名特别政治股人员及日本宪兵队一行人与本人、副督察长 Vung Ts Ming 以及刑事调查处（C.I.）所属侦探于当晚10时在虹口西捕房会合。

在约定时间，本人在虹口西捕房会见了 D. J. Yamahara 以及由 Kitoda 军曹率领的一队宪兵，并在调派三名华籍巡警后，前往上述地址。

抵达后发现，该地址是一栋大宅，屋主显然是一位较为富有的华人。

本人询问了一位长者，Zung Ping Ki（陳丙麒）先生，他表示被通缉者（其弟）已离开上海。

由于日本宪兵队坚持要搜查书面证据，遂对被通缉者的房间进行了搜查。然而，未发现任何

were, however, found. Whilst on the premises D.S.I. Tung
Ts Ming ascertained that considerable strife had been going
on between certain members of the family for a number of years.
This had been the subject of litigation, and negotiations
between the litigants or friends of the family had been going
on, and sums of money had been paid in an effort to settle
this trouble.

Brother I Yang Mu, whilst Garrison Commander of Shanghai
had attempted to bring about the arrest of the said man,
on a charge of being a "Traitor", but on this being brought
to the notice of the S.M.P. this contemplated action was
suppressed.

It is now suspected that one of the disgruntled litigants
has caused false information to be placed with the Japanese
authorities in the hope of bringing about his arrest.

On leaving the premises, the party, at the request of
the Gendarmerie, proceeded to Louza Police Station, where
on assistance being rendered by Sub-Inspector Bell, the wanted
man's offices, The "Dong Oo Koong" (同和公) Shipping Hong,
1st floor, House No.9 Lane No.389 Hanko Road was visited.

A search of these offices failed to reveal any trace of
the wanted man, or any incriminating evidence.

The undersigned has now requested D.S.I. Umemoto to ask
Sergt. Major Katoda to obtain a written statement from their
informant.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH 9/5/38）

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,

〔此处签名潦草〕

D. I.

任何定罪文件。在现场期间，副督察长 Tung Ts Ming 获悉，该家庭某些成员之间多年来一直存在严重不和。此事曾引发诉讼，诉讼双方或家族友人之间一直在进行谈判，并支付款项试图平息纠纷。

其兄 I Yang Mu 在担任上海卫戍司令期间，曾试图以“汉奸”罪名逮捕此人，但此事引起工部局警务处注意后，该预定行动被制止。

现怀疑其中一名不满的诉讼当事人向日本当局提供了虚假情报，以期促成其被捕。

离开该处后，应宪兵队要求，一行人前往老闸捕房，在副巡官 Bell 的协助下，走访了被通缉者的办公地点，即汉口路389弄9号一楼的“同和公”（Dong Oo Koong）轮船行。

对该办公室的搜查未能发现被通缉者的任何踪迹，也未发现任何定罪证据。

本人现已请求 D.S.I. Umemoto 请 Katoda 军曹从其线人处获取一份书面陈述。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处特别股 1938年5月9日）

此致，
敬礼，

〔此处签名潦草〕

D. I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. ____
S.1 Special Branch. ____
REPORT
Date August 8, 1938.
Subject Visit to House 7, Lane 831, Tiendong Road by the Municipal
Police.
Made by D. S. Pitts Forwarded by ____

（批：On information furnished by J.S.D.C.）

At 11.15 a.m. August 8, 1938 members of the Special
Branch accompanied by detectives from West Hongkew Station
visited House No. 7, Lane 831, Tiendong Road for the purpose
of searching for and seizing anti-Japanese literature which was
suspected of being housed on the premises.

Upon arrival it was learned that these premises had
been searched during the evening of August 7 by a party from
the Japanese Gendarmerie in the company of detectives from
Crime Branch Headquarters and uniformed men from West Hongkew
Station, but nothing of an incriminating nature had been found.

The D.C. (Special Branch) was acquainted with these
facts by telephone and he ordered that this morning's search
immediately cease.

（批：C12 / 8）
（批：S.J.D.C. See.）

The owner of the premises, Mr. Zung Ping Chi (陳炳麒),
is the proprietor of the Dong Woo Loong Shipping Company, 9/389
Hankow Road. He is quite well known in local circles as being
a very respectable person with no political affiliations. He
was not present at the time of this morning's police visit, but
it was learned that after the Japanese Gendarmerie had searched
his home yesterday evening, a subsequent call was paid to his
office on Hankow Road by these officers.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE COMMISSIONER'S OFFICE 10 AUG. 1933）
（印：SPECIAL DEPUTY COMMISSIONER HOUSE 10 AUG. 1933 S.M.POLICE）

Enquiries among the many inmates of the Tiendong Road
house revealed that the most probable source of the Japanese
information was one Woo Kwang (胡光), a "high class" loafer
residing in the West Hongkew district. He has received finan-
cial assistance over a long period from various members of
Zung's family, but his recent requests for more aid have been
rejected. During the past few days, numerous telephone calls
from Woo Kwang have been received by Zung's family warning

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 ____
S.1 特别股。____
报告
日期：1938年8月8日。
事由：市政警察走访天潼路831弄7号。
撰写人：D. S. Pitts 转呈人：____

（批注：依据 J.S.D.C. 提供的情报。）

1938年8月8日上午11时15分，特别股成员在虹口西捕房侦探的陪同下，走访了天潼路831弄7号，目的是搜查并扣押疑似藏匿于该处的反日文献。

抵达后得知，8月7日晚，日本宪兵队一行人在刑事调查处总部侦探及虹口西捕房制服警员的陪同下已搜查过该处，但未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。

特别股副主任（D.C.）通过电话获悉这些情况，并命令立即停止今早的搜查。

（批注：C12 / 8）
（批注：S.J.D.C. 秘书。）

该处业主 Zung Ping Chi（陳炳麒）先生是汉口路389/9号东武隆轮船公司（Dong Woo Loong Shipping Company）的所有人。他在当地圈子里颇有名气，被视为一位无可挑剔、无政治派系背景的体面人士。今早警察走访时他不在场，但据悉，昨晚日本宪兵队搜查其住所后，这些官员随后又去了他在汉口路的办公室。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处处长办公室 1933年8月10日）
（印章：副总督察长寓所 1933年8月10日 工部局警务处）

对天潼路住宅内众多住户的查询显示，日本方面情报的最可能来源是一名叫 Woo Kwang（胡光）的人，他是居住在虹口区的一名“高等”游手好闲之徒。长期以来，他一直从 Zung 家族的不同成员那里获得经济资助，但他最近要求更多援助的请求遭到了拒绝。在过去几天里，Zung 家族接到 Woo Kwang 打来的多次电话，警告

the master that something might happen in the near future
to endanger his life. A similar message was again received
during the morning of August 7 from Woo Kwang.

These activities would appear to be the result
of the refusal of Zung and his family to continue "making
gifts" to Woo Kwang. This belief is to a great extent
corroborated by the fact that Woo Kwang was observed sitting
in the car used by the Japanese Gendarmerie during their
visit to 7/831 Tiendong Road last night. He was seen by
Mr. Zung Nyi Shing (陳義鏗), a nephew of the owner of the
house.

D. C. (Special Branch)

Commons
Sir,
In an endeavour to stop
this sort of thing, D.C. Div has
issued instructions to D.O.s
that in all instances where
Japanese Authorities seek assistance
to search for literature, the party
carrying out the search must
include representatives of S.B. Branch
(one foreign & one Chinese minimum)

〔此处有手写签名：Jno Robertson〕
D.C. (SB)
